full_judgment:
Kazi Md. Ejarul Haque Akondo, J: This Rule Nisi at the instance of the petitioners, on an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the seniority list dated 3-12-2017 issued and published under the joint signature of respondent Nos. 5-7 thereunder prepared a list of seniority of Deputy Directors under the Finance Pool of Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) and Clause-3 of Office Order No. 390/2005 dated 12-5-2005 issued by respondent No.4 in appointing the petitioners and others in the post of Assistant Director (Accounts/Finance/Audit), Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (Annexure- 'A' & "G") should not be declared to be illegal without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. It has been stated that the service of the petitioners and other employees of BIWTA is being regulated by the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority Employees Service Regulations, 1990 (In short. BIWTA Service Regulations, 1990) [Annexure-F]. But respondent NOs. 5-7 in violation of its regulation 10(1) and the judgments of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh most illegally and arbitrarily under their joint signatures prepared and published the impugned seniority list of Deputy Directors under the Finance Pool of BIWTA on 3-12-2017 (Annexure-G). 

 4. It has further been stated that BIWTA earlier violated the provision of regulation 10(1) of the BIWTA Service Regulations. 1990, and by Office Order No. 709 of 1999 dated 25-8-1999 published a seniority list. And being aggrieved by the said seniority list Mr. Sadiqul Islam, Deputy Assistant Director (Survey), Hydrographic Department, BIWTA filed Writ Petition No. 4332 of 1999 before this Court and obtained a Rule Nisi thereon. After hearing the same, this Court by judgment and order dated 8-12-2004 made the Rule absolute and directed the respondents to prepare a fresh seniority list as per the observations made in the judgment. It was observed in the judgment that "We have already delivered a judgment in Writ Petition No. 5587 of 2020 heard along with Writ Petition No. 94 of 2003 in which it was held in a similar situation like this that sub-Rule-1 of Rule-10 shall apply for determination of inter seniority of employees". Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order BIWTA preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 348 of 2005 before the Apex Court. which was dismissed on 22-6-2006 (Annexure-I), wherein it was held that "the contention of the writ petition is that his seniority is to be continued from the date of joining in the terms of regulation 10(1) of the BIWTA Service Regulations, 1990 and regulation 10(2) shall not apply in his case as no merit list was prepared by any selection committee for their appointment." According to the above-stated judgment the BIWTA by its Office Order No. 1639 of 2006 dated 28-8-2006 canceled the seniority list dated 25-8-1999 and published a fresh seniority list on considering seniority based on joining (Annexure-J). 

 17. The learned Advocate for the petitioners contends that BIWTA earlier violated the provision of regulation 10(1) of the BIWTA Service Regulations, 1990, and published a seniority list on 25-8-1999. Being aggrieved by the same, one Mr. Sadiqul Islam, Deputy Assistant Director filed Writ Petition No. 4332 of 1999, wherein the Rule was made absolute with a direction upon the respondents to prepare a fresh seniority list as per the observations made in the judgment. Being aggrieved by the said judgment dated 8-12-2004, BIWTA preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 348 of 2005 before the Apex Court, which was dismissed on 22-6-2006 (Annexure-I). In the judgment it was held that the seniority of the writ petitioner is to be continued from the date of joining in terms of regulation 10(1) of the BIWTA Service Regulations, 1990 and its regulation 10(2) shall not apply in his case as no merit list was prepared by any selection committee for their appointment. Under the above-stated judgment the BIWTA by its office order dated 28-8-2006 canceled the earlier seniority list dated 25-8-1999 and published a fresh seniority list (Annexure-J). The service of the employees of BIWTA is regulated under the BIWTA Service Regulations, 1990 but the respondents violated the said regulations and imposed clause-3 in appointment Order No. 390/2005 dated 12-5-2005 of the petitioners (Annexure-A). 

 23. From the above, it appears that a Recruitment Committee was duly constituted by the BIWTA which after completion of selection finally published the merit list of 08 candidates for appointment in the post of Assistant Director including the petitioners (Annexures-i and x). And respondent No.2 filed the said merit list including the marks sheet before this Court in a proper manner. But for non-filing of the mark sheet of petitioner No.1 for the reason of its non-finding cannot vitiate the entire merit list (Annexures-i and x) after 17 years of its preparation. However, the petitioners nowhere in the writ petition denied the merit list; rather the learned Advocate for the petitioners contends that the petitioners have reasons to believe that they secured top positions in the merit list.
